problems.title: Common solution of three conditions
problems.question: Find the common solution of $\sqrt{2x-1}<7$, $\sqrt{3x-20}>-1$, and $x^2-9x+14=0$.
problems.idea: Use domains, exact identities, and the relevant geometric relations.
formulas: The first condition gives $1/2\le x<25$. The second is automatic on its domain $x\ge20/3$.
steps: The quadratic factors as(x−2)(x−7)=0. Only 7 lies in the joint interval[20/3,25).

problems.title: Domains select signs before simplification
problems.question: Evaluate $-x\sqrt{-x^3y^2}(\sqrt{xy}/\sqrt{-x^2y}-1/\sqrt{-x^5y^2})$ if x²+x=6 and y²=4.
problems.idea: Use domains, exact identities, and the relevant geometric relations.
formulas: The algebraic possibilities are x=2,−3 and y=2,−2. Nonzero square-root denominators force x<0 and y<0, hence x=−3, y=−2.
steps: Set u=−x>0, v=−y>0. The prefactor is u²√u·v. Inside the parentheses the first term is √(uv)/(u√v)=1/√u, and the second is 1/(u²√u·v). Multiplication therefore gives u²v−1.

problems.title: Reconstruct a triangle from three interior points
problems.question: M lies on AB with AM: MB=1:3. N, K are the midpoints of BC, AC. Only M, N, K remain drawn. Construct ABC with compass and straightedge.
problems.idea: Use domains, exact identities, and the relevant geometric relations.
formulas: The midpoint theorem gives $\overrightarrow{KN}=\tfrac12\overrightarrow{AB}$. Put $v=\tfrac12\overrightarrow{KN}$; then $A=M-v,B=M+3v,C=2K-A$.
steps: Construct the midpoint of KN to obtain length KN/2. Through M construct the parallel to KN. On it mark A one such length opposite direction K→N, and B three such lengths in direction K→N. These are standard compass length transfers and parallel-line constructions.
Reflect A in K to obtain C: draw AK and extend it beyond K by KA. Then K is midpoint of AC. Because AB=2KN and is parallel to KN, N=(B+C)/2. Also AM is one quarter of AB, verifying AM: MB=1:3.
problems.answer: This constructs the unique labelled triangle ABC, as shown in the diagram.

problems.title: Square roots of squares
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt{x^2-6x+9}=|2\sqrt3-3|$.
problems.idea: Use domains, exact identities, and the relevant geometric relations.
formulas: The left side is $|x-3|$. Since $2\sqrt3>3$, the right side is $2\sqrt3-3$.
steps: Thus x−3=±(2√3−3). Add 3 in each case.

problems.title: A diameter creates a right angle
problems.question: AB=BC=10. The circle with diameter AB meets BC at D with BD: DC=4:1. Find D’s distance from AC.
problems.idea: Use domains, exact identities, and the relevant geometric relations.
steps: In right triangle ADC, AC=√(6²+2²)=2√10 and are a=6·2/2=6. If the requested altitude is h, also are a=AC·h/2. Thus h=12/(2√10)=3√10/5.

problems.title: Triangle from two tangent circles
problems.question: Circles of radii 3 and 9 touch externally at C. A common external tangent touches them at A, B. Find triangle ABC’s sides.
problems.idea: Use domains, exact identities, and the relevant geometric relations.
formulas: The centre distance is 12. Perpendicular radii to the common tangent differ by 6, so $AB=\sqrt{12^2-6^2}=6\sqrt3$.
steps: Take A=(0,0), B=(6√3,0), with centres O₁=(0,3), O₂=(6√3,9). Since O₁C=3 of the total 12, C=O₁+(O₂−O₁)/4=(3√3/2,9/2).
Then AC²=27/4+81/4=27, and BC²=243/4+81/4=81. Take positive square roots.

problems.title: Compare large expressions by simple bounds
problems.question: Compare $S=8/(2026+8+199)+199/(8+199+2025)+2025/(199+2025+2026)+2026/(2025+2026+8)$ with $T=\sqrt{[(8/199+2025/2026)^2+(199/8+2026/2025)^2]/2}$.
problems.idea: Use domains, exact identities, and the relevant geometric relations.
formulas: Every summand of S is positive and less than 1, so $S<4$. Let $v=199/8+2026/2025$; then $T\ge v/\sqrt2$.
steps: v>199/8>24. Consequently T>24/√2=12√2>4. Combining the strict bounds gives S<4<T, without needing decimal approximations.
problems.answer: The second expression is strictly greater.
